# @eltonbautista/vue

Cabinet is a small, playful Vue 3 component library with an arcade-cabinet feel and a tested accessibility contract on every component.

**Components:** `CabButton`, `CabTextField`, `CabCheckbox`, `CabSwitch`, `CabSelect`, `CabTabs`, `CabDialog`, `CabCard`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @eltonbautista/vue @eltonbautista/tokens
```

```ts
// main.ts
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/tokens.css'   // design tokens (CSS custom properties)
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/fonts.css'    // Sora + Outfit (optional)
import '@eltonbautista/vue/style.css'       // component styles
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabButton, CabTextField } from '@eltonbautista/vue'
const email = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <CabTextField v-model="email" label="Email" type="email" />
  <CabButton>Book a seat</CabButton>
</template>
```

## Accessibility

Every component follows a WAI-ARIA APG pattern and documents its keyboard map, focus behaviour and screen-reader output. Each one is tested in a real browser for keyboard interaction and axe violations. See the Storybook docs for each component's Accessibility section.

content.text:
The landing page is in `src/App.vue`, and `npm run build` passes with no errors. I haven't run it in a browser or tested it with a screen reader or axe, so the accessibility and keyboard behaviour below comes from the components' documented contract and my own reading of the code.

- **Title and intro:** the page has a skip link, an `<h1>` and a short intro paragraph.
- **Track cards:** the three tracks are `CabCard`s linking to `/tracks/board`, `/tracks/digital` and `/tracks/larp`. The card's title is the link and its hit area stretches over the whole card, so clicking anywhere on it navigates. For keyboard users that is one tab stop per card.
- **Sign-up form:**
  - **Fields:** name, email, experience level and the code-of-conduct checkbox.
  - **Validation:** it runs on submit. Errors appear on the fields, and focus moves to the first invalid one. The code of conduct has to be ticked, or the form shows an error and doesn't submit.
  - **Submit button:** I left it enabled rather than disabled until the checkbox is ticked. A disabled button gives people no explanation of what is wrong.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that saves on every toggle, with no save button. It stores the setting in `localStorage` (an assumption, since there is no backend) and announces "Email reminders turned on/off. Saved." in a live region.
- **Confirmation:** a valid submit opens a `CabDialog` summarising name, email and level, with "Go back" and "Confirm booking" buttons. Confirming shows a success message and moves focus to its heading.

`CabCheckbox` has no `error` prop, so the code-of-conduct error is a separate `role="alert"` paragraph rather than being tied to the checkbox itself.

The route links are plain `href`s, so they will 404 until those pages exist.
